description: Live V6 evidence: pan-reviewer reviews the same executed phase five times (exec-phase's code_review step, recorded in the findings ledger each time), then the engine reports the reviewer's findings churn across the five reports.
why: Program V6's evidence gate: churn over five live repeated reviews. Findings close only on evidence and keep stable ids, so a judge whose findings appear and vanish while the code does not change is not measuring the code. The seed's diff carries two real defects (an off-by-one bulk threshold, an unknown code priced as NaN). The churn figure is a measurement, not a pass mark: the scenario passes when all five reviews were recorded and the figure exists; read the rate from the last step's JSON in report.json.

steps.why: Phase 1's work lands as its own commits on top of the seed, so the review has a base and a non-empty diff.
The engine finds the phase base and src/cart.js in scope: without it the reviewer would be handed nothing to review.

steps.prompt: Review phase 1 of this project exactly as the `code_review` step of `.claude/pan-wizard-core/workflows/exec-phase.md` says, steps 1 to 4 only: collect the review scope, collect the reviewer's open findings on phase 1, spawn the pan-reviewer agent with them, save its report verbatim to `.planning/phases/01-cart-total/01-review.md`, and record it with `findings record --phase 1 --agent pan-reviewer`. This is an unattended run: do not fix anything, do not edit source files, do not dispose of any finding, and do not go on to verification. End by printing the verdict the record returned.
steps.why: One review of the unchanged diff by pan-reviewer, recorded in the findings ledger. Repeated five times on the same code, the ids that appear and disappear between reports are the churn V6 measures.
